summary: G. B. Beaman (1870–1942) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cincinnati (B.A. ~1889–1893), the University of Jena (1893), and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1894–1895), where he was taught by Ernst Windisch in 1894.

G. B. Palsule (1920–2007) worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
Indologist G. Herberich studied under Julius Jolly at the University of Würzburg, where he completed his Ph.D. by 1893.
G. K. Jenkins (1918–2005) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Bloxham School (~1932–1937) and held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera (1899–1973), an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from the University of London and SOAS, studying under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He taught at University College, Colombo and became Dean at the University of Ceylon.

Active in Buddhist studies, G. Rita Dudley-Grant studied at NHS Grampian (1983–1986) and Robert Gordon University (1994–1997). She held posts at Virgin Islands Behavioral Sciences (attested 2003) and as an advanced practitioner physiotherapist at NHS Grampian (2004).

Working in Indology and philosophy, G. S. Sahay studied at the University of Nebraska Medical Center (2005–2009). He served as a Research Officer at Kaivalyadhama (attested 2005), did a postdoc at MIT (2010–2014), and became Professor at Oregon State University (2023).
G. Srinivasa Murti, who worked in Indology, served as the Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre, a post attested for the periods 1938–1949 and 1971.

After earning a bachelor's degree at Yale (~1951–1955), G. Thomas Tanselle taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978–2006), while also serving as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006).
G. V. Aston, a scholar in philosophy and religious studies, studied under Paul Harrison at the University of Canterbury, completing a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy between 1986 and 2004.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945, later retiring as Senior Epigraphical Assistant from the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso was a scholar who studied under both the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Gabriel Engelsmann (1858–1924) was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna by 1885.

Gabriel Jouveau-Dubreuil (1885–1945) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He taught physics and chemistry at Lycée Français de Pondichéry in 1909 and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Paris (~1912–1914).

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, later holding the Chair of Buddhist Studies at Kyoto University from 1935 to 1971.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She completed her studies at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied with traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Galuh Nur Fattah, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed an M.Phil. at Gadjah Mada University (2021–2023). He served as an assistant professor at Gadjah Mada University (2024–2025) and became a lecturer at STABN Raden Wijaya in 2025.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of Washington. A scholar of religious and Buddhist studies, he taught at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University, retiring from Princeton in 2000.

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. Working in Indology and history/archaeology, he held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905), the University of Calcutta (~1914–1918), and Banaras Hindu University (~1918–1923).

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Calcutta, and Allahabad. He served as professor at Muir Central College, principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and vice chancellor of Allahabad University.
